text:
Declan Carlile came to Pittsburgh from Tampa Bay with 46 NHL games behind him, and he's already played 21 for the Penguins, about 18 minutes a night. For an undrafted defenseman, that's a real opportunity.

The points are light: three goals and six points, one point in his last ten. But our numbers say he's been one of the unluckiest players in the league. The Penguins have scored 9.6 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five on five they take 52% of the expected goals in his minutes, roughly the same as without him. His talent range suggests the scoring rate he's at now is close to his ceiling, so the luck matters more for the team than for his line.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man last season (86th percentile among defensemen in primary shot assists) with a weak spot on exits (31% with possession).

The Penguins have won three of his last ten. What to watch: whether the on-ice goals start matching the chances. That swing would help everyone on the team.
